behavior: Active foliage gleaner that hops and flits through outer leaves and slender branches, usually high in the canopy, taking caterpillars and other invertebrates. It often joins mixed-species foraging flocks outside the breeding season and may also eat fruit and nectar.
field_marks: Small, compact body with a short tail
Gray-olive head with a pale eyebrow and dark eye
Olive to yellow-green back and wings with weak or absent wingbars
White undertail coverts contrasting with dusky legs and tail
habitat: Breeds in young or middle-aged boreal coniferous and mixed forests, especially areas with openings, dense shrubs, or boggy ground. During migration it uses many wooded habitats, groves, and brush; in winter it occupies open or semiopen tropical broadleaf and second-growth forests, including shade-grown plantations.
